name: One-Side-First Substitution Bound
statement: Under the common-section interval hypothesis, for each $b\in\{0,1\}$, $\sigma(C\circ_iT)\leq\max\{\sigma(C_b),\sigma(C_{1-b};H),\sigma_{\square}(F_b),\sigma(F_{1-b})\}$. If both test sides are dismantlable ample, this becomes $\sigma(C\circ_iT)\leq\min_b\max\{\sigma(C_b),\sigma(C_{1-b};H)\}$.
proof: First use rectangular extension to order $(C_b\times F_b)\cup(H\times\{0,1\}^Y)$ beginning with $C_b\times F_b$. Then append the exclusive fibers of the other side in an optimal $H$-first order. Same-fiber and same-side predecessors use inner and outer witnesses. An opposite-side predecessor is replaced through a point of $H$ in its coordinate interval, giving a contained pure outer disagreement. If both test sides have width zero, their cube-completion widths equal zero, and minimizing over the first side gives the second formula.
